First printed edition located: Sergio Ramírez (ed.), El pensamiento vivo de Sandino (San José: EDUCA, 1974; Managua: Nueva Nicaragua, 1984, vol. 1, no. 111, pp. 341-355). Keep 1929 as the work's date, but label it 'written'.

considered.work: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz, Loa para el auto sacramental de El divino Narciso (1690)
considered.reason: Its allegory (América, Occidente, Religión, Celo) is about the conversion of the Mexica and the continuity between their rites and the Eucharist: it fits. The Respuesta a sor Filotea (1691, printed 1700) is about a woman's right to learning, not the New World: it does not fit the period's theme. PD (d. 1695); Project Gutenberg #74087 has Obras selectas; Wikisource has the Respuesta (not checked for the Loa).

considered.work: Bernardino de Sahagún, Historia general de las cosas de Nueva España (c. 1577; first printed 1829-1830)
considered.reason: Fits the theme, but its Florentine Codex is already one of the pillar paintings; bilingual Nahuatl-Spanish and huge. A good later addition.

considered.work: Recopilación de leyes de los reynos de las Indias (1680)
considered.reason: A law code rather than a work of thought; Solórzano (P07) is its doctrinal companion.

corrections.source: Front matter of El antimperialismo y el Apra, Fondo Editorial del Congreso del Perú, 2010 (https://www.marxists.org/espanol/haya/1930s/antimperialismo/index.htm): first edition Dec 1935; Ercilla 1936 is the 2nd ed. (Penn and SIU catalogue records say '2. ed.').
Title as printed in the 1936 Ercilla edition and the 2010 Congress edition.
Editorial note in Geopolítica(s) 12(2) 2021 citing Ramírez, El pensamiento vivo (1974; 1984 ed. no. 111); García Laguardia published it as 'documento inédito'.

notes: Archive.org holds many private uploads of modern, in-copyright editions (e.g. Vasconcelos, Maeztu reprints, Haya). Only institutional scans (John Carter Brown, Robarts/Toronto, Universidad de Sevilla, Wellcome, Princeton) or the Internet Archive's own lending library are cited as legitimate.
HathiTrust 'US access only' items are PD in the US but HathiTrust blocks them outside the US; Beltrán/Carlos in Europe will not see them without a US connection.
None of the 25 works T026-T050 has a ready clean transcription except Mariátegui (Wikisource / marxists.org) and Sandino (Geopolítica(s)); the rest need OCR from scans.
Wikisource (es) was checked by API for every PD title: only Mariátegui is there among T026-T050.
